subject: Prospective PhD applicant (Fall 2027): how people make sense of apps that use their data
body:
Dear Professor Li,

I'm a product data analyst at a consumer fitness app, and I'm applying to the Khoury HCI PhD program for Fall 2027. I'm writing because my interests seem to overlap with the PEACH Lab's work, and I'd like to know whether you're taking new students this cycle.

At work I analyzed the launch of an AI feature that rewrites people's workout plans using their sleep, activity and heart-rate data. By our metrics it worked. But in the post-launch survey, about one in ten people said some version of "it changed my plan and I don't know why," and a couple of them turned off health-data sharing afterward. In user interviews, you could hear people guessing at what the app was doing with their data and whether they could still steer it. That's what I want to study: what people think is happening when an app uses their data to make choices for them, and what makes them feel they still have a say.

My background is mostly quantitative: four years of running and analyzing product experiments, plus undergraduate HCI coursework in interviews and usability testing. I don't have publications yet. I'm happy to send my CV.

Would you be open to a short call? Or is there anything you'd recommend I read before applying?

Thanks for your time,
Riley Nakamura
riley.nakamura@example.com
